➡️How can you handle missing data in PySpark?

Handling missing data in PySpark is crucial for maintaining data integrity. PySpark provides various ways to handle missing values using DataFrame API functions like .fillna(), .dropna(), and .replace(). Below are common methods:

▶️1. Dropping Missing Values

⚡Use .dropna() to remove rows with missing values.
⚡You can specify a subset of columns to consider for missing values.
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col

# Initialize Spark Session
spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("MissingDataHandling").getOrCreate()

# Sample DataFrame with missing values
data = [(1, "Alice", None), (2, None, 50), (3, "Bob", 30), (4, None, None)]
columns = ["ID", "Name", "Age"]
df = spark.createDataFrame(data, columns)

# Drop rows where all columns are NULL
df_drop_all = df.dropna(how="all") 

# Drop rows where any column is NULL
df_drop_any = df.dropna(how="any") 

# Drop rows where only a specific column is NULL
df_drop_subset = df.dropna(subset=["Name"]) 

df_drop_any.show()

▶️2. Filling Missing Values

⚡Use .fillna() to replace null values with specific values.
⚡You can provide different values for different columns.
# Fill missing values with a default value
df_fill = df.fillna({"Name": "Unknown", "Age": 0})

df_fill.show()

▶️3. Replacing Missing Values with Other Values
⚡.replace() can replace None (null) values with a specific value
⚡df_replace = df.replace(None, "N/A")
df_replace.show()

▶️4. Using na Functions

⚡PySpark provides df.na as an alias for handling missing values.
df.na.drop().show() # Equivalent to df.dropna()
df.na.fill("Unknown", subset=["Name"]).show()
df.na.replace(None, "No Data").show()

▶️5. Using SQL Functions for More Control
⚡You can use SQL functions to replace nulls dynamically.
from pyspark.sql.functions import when

df_new = df.withColumn("Age", when(col("Age").isNull(), 25).otherwise(col("Age")))
df_new.show()
